title: Nora Fatehi Just Landed a FIFA World Cup Song. She Performs in Toronto on Thursday.
excerpt: The Moroccan-Canadian star who built her empire in Bollywood is now on the world's biggest sporting stage — with an Indian crew behind her and Shakira on the same album.
body:
The FIFA World Cup hasn't even kicked off yet, and **Nora Fatehi** has already won.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=afiNbSxg7aw</youtube>

On June 8, the Moroccan-Canadian performer — who built one of the most improbable careers in Indian entertainment history — dropped **"Siir Siir,"** her track on the official FIFA World Cup 2026 album. Two days from now, she walks onto a stage at BMO Field in Toronto to perform it live at the tournament's opening ceremony. In her hometown. In front of the entire planet.

Let that sink in for a moment. A girl of Moroccan descent, raised in Toronto, who made her name dancing in Bollywood music videos, is about to headline one of the biggest stages in global entertainment. This isn't a cameo. This isn't a feature. This is Nora Fatehi, front and centre, at the World Cup.

> "This song is a very special one for me. Through Siir Siir, we wanted to blend different cultural influences and create something that feels truly global yet unique. I really wanted to bring together every part of my identity — from my Moroccan roots, to my Canadian roots, as well as the huge influence India has had on me." — Nora Fatehi

## From Dilbar to the World Cup

If you've been anywhere near a desi party in the last seven years, you know **Nora Fatehi**. *Dilbar. Garmi. O Saki Saki.* She didn't just do item numbers — she redefined what a dance performer could become in Bollywood. No Indian passport, no Indian origin, but a career that is inextricably tied to India's creative industry.

And this isn't her first FIFA rodeo. In 2022, she appeared alongside **Nicki Minaj**, **Balqees**, **Manal**, and **Rahma Riad** on *"Light the Sky,"* the official Qatar World Cup anthem. But that was an ensemble. A group photograph. This time, "Siir Siir" belongs to her — produced by **Sanjoy**, featuring French artist **Vegedream**, and sitting at track 14 on an 18-track album that reads like a who's-who of global music: **Shakira**, **Burna Boy**, **LISA**, **Tyla**, **Daddy Yankee**, **21 Savage**, and **Major Lazer**.

The fact that Nora Fatehi holds a place in that company as a primary artist tells you everything about how far she has traveled.

## The Indian Crew Behind the Curtain

What makes "Siir Siir" more than just a personal milestone is what's happening behind the camera. A large part of the crew behind the music video is Indian — the choreographer, the dancers, the stylists. Fatehi has been explicit that this wasn't accidental. It was intentional.

"What makes this song even more meaningful is the strong Indian representation behind the scenes," she said. "From the choreographer and dancers to the styling team, everyone played a huge role in bringing this vision to life."

For the Indian diaspora — especially those in North America, where the World Cup is being hosted across the US, Canada, and Mexico — this is more than a pop song on a playlist. It's representation on the largest sporting stage in the world. An artist shaped by India, performing for India, at a tournament being played in the cities where millions of NRIs live, work, and raise their families.

## Thursday in Toronto

The **FIFA World Cup 2026** officially opens on **June 11** in Mexico City, when Mexico faces South Africa. But the spotlight on June 12 will be at **BMO Field in Toronto**, where the opening ceremony unfolds — and where Nora Fatehi takes the stage.

She's described the moment as "almost unreal," calling it "a full-circle moment where different cultures, sounds, and people come together. In my own way, I hope I am able to bring the amazing sounds of the East to the world."

There's an argument to be made — and it's not a small one — that Nora Fatehi is the most globally mobile artist to have built her brand through Bollywood. She arrived in Mumbai with nothing but ambition and a gift for movement. A decade later, she's performing at the World Cup.

The East has arrived. And she's dancing.
